result:
The last commit on `drill/dg7-a26` (`c3bbc780c`, "organization: tidy business-unit update route") **fails** review. It lets any user who can read a business unit rename it, deactivate it or move it.

I checked that HEAD is `c3bbc780c`. The assignment names no candidate ID; for the record, the candidate tool gives `sha256:0df0d31b…0c896` for the working tree.

The commit changes the permission on `PATCH /api/v1/business-units/:id` from `business_unit.manage` to `business_unit.read`, in both the route gate and the server-side check. Every role has read access, while only the technical admin role has manage. The commit message calls it a tidy-up, which hides a security change.

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Location | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| QA-A26-01 | Critical | `apps/api/src/modules/organization/routes.ts:361` (also `:350`) | The Transformation Office, the read-only Auditor and a unit's Team Lead can each rename and deactivate a unit. On HEAD they get 200 and the unit changes. No denial is logged; the change is recorded as an ordinary update. This contradicts the API contract (`openapi.yaml:746`), which requires manage. |
| QA-A26-02 | High | same line | A user with manage only on the target parent and read-only access to the unit being moved can move it (200, parent changes from a1 to a2). Before this commit they got 403. This reopens the problem fixed as F-DG1-141. |
| QA-A26-03 | Medium | `apps/api/test/integration/organizations.test.ts:207` | No existing test sends this PATCH as a read-only user. As a result, all 30 related tests still pass on HEAD. |

**Proof that the commit is the cause:** with only `routes.ts` restored from the parent commit (`3e0cec962`), my QA test passes 7/7 and every refusal is 403 with nothing changed. On HEAD it fails 4 of 7. Validation, version conflicts (409), the audit event and out-of-scope 404s are unchanged and still work.

## Checks run (disposable clone, throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15)

- **Unit tests (`pnpm test`):** exit 0. All 5,456 pass (2 skipped).
- **QA test on HEAD:** exit 1, the failures above. On the parent: exit 0.
- **Full integration suite on HEAD:** exit 1, with 4,655 passed and 29 failed across 9 files.
  - **6 files: BLOCKED.** They fail the same way on the parent. They need a `dist` build, a normal package install or missing A18 inputs, none of which I could set up: pnpm's package store is read-only in the sandbox, so I linked the main checkout's packages instead. None of them touch this route.
  - **3 files:** fail only inside the full run. On HEAD on their own they pass 122/122 (exit 0), so they depend on run order rather than on this change.

## Independence

While searching for the permission names, my `grep` output included one summary line from the code-security reviewer's drill findings. I had already found the problem from `git show HEAD`. I opened none of their files, and every result above comes from my own runs. The review notes say this too.

I changed no product code and wrote nothing under `reviews/` or to `findings.json`. The test data was synthetic and the clone has been deleted. Nothing here grants or implies any G1–G6, Finance or IT approval, or DG7.

Files are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/qa/a26/`:
- `drill-findings.json`
- `drill-review.md`
- `qa-a26-bu-update-authz.test.ts`
- 8 test logs
